spatial_entity.notes: Royal construction-project context in Umma province; exact archaeological location remains unknown.

claim.summary: The Garshana construction project employed many hundreds of enslaved and hired workers; the archive presents enslaved labour as an ongoing, regular component of the workforce, with household slaves engaged in craft production, laundering, construction and related work.

territorial_practice.notes: P3 is restricted to the bounded Garshana institutional/workplace context, not mechanically generalized to the entire Ur III population.

source.title: Slavery and Freedom in the Third Dynasty of Ur: Implications of the Garshana Archives
source.author_or_institution: Robert McC. Adams / Cuneiform Digital Library Initiative
source.independence_notes: Specialist synthesis based on the Garshana archive and prior Assyriological scholarship.
source.reliability_limitations: Garshana's exact location is unknown; status terminology and boundaries between slavery and other dependency remain complex.

evidence.evidence_role: specialist interpretation of workforce and status

source.title: Slavery in Third-Millennium Mesopotamia: An Overview of Sources and Studies
source.independence_notes: Independent specialist overview of third-millennium Mesopotamian slavery and forced/bonded labour.
source.reliability_limitations: Broad regional synthesis; not specific to Garshana prevalence.

version.version_label: IRIS repository record for Journal of Global Slavery 3 (2018)

geometry.resolution_method: The Garshana archive places the project in Umma province, probably near Zabalam, but the exact site has not been securely located.
